History of Present Illness:
___ yo female with hx of ESRD on HD, PVD s/p bilateral BKAs, and 
hx of atrial flutter presented to OSH with episode of SOB. On 
the morning of ___ the patient noted a relatively acute 
onset of palpitations and shortness of breath with associated 
diaphoresis. The episode apparently lasted approximately 15 
minutes. She denies chest pain or chest pressure. EMS was called 
and vitals at that time showed a BP of 240/140, a HR of 130 and 
an O2 sat of 80%. She was given nitro and oxygen which relieved 
some of her symptoms. She was brought to ___ and on 
presentation had elevated troponins to 2.25 and a BNP of 2897. 
EKG at that time showed NSR with LVH and LAH with no ST 
elevations. She was begun on a heparin drip and admitted to 
their ICU. She underwent emergent dialysis for acute pulmonary 
edema which significantly improved her dyspnea. Her troponins 
began to trend down. However, on ___ she developed episodes of 
atrial flutter with rates to the 140s. She was asympomtatic 
during these periods but she did have a subsequent increase of 
her previously falling troponins. These episodes were controlled 
with IV metoprolol and an increased PO dose. Of note the patient 
had recently been started on Diltiazem as an outpatient which 
was not noted or given at the OSH. She underwent an adenosine 
stress MIBI on ___ which by report showed no regional WMA, 
an EF of 43% and no perfusion defects. A TTE done on the same 
day showed sever LVH, with a septum measuring 1.9cm, an EF of 
60%, heavy mitral calcification, and no focal WMA. At this time 
her heparin was stopped given the negative MIBI and she was sent 
to ___ for further evaluation and possible catheterization, as 
her outpatient cardiologist is here. Prior to this episode she 
denies any episodes of chest pain, DOE, SOB, syncope, 
presyncope.

CXR:
Cardiac silhouette is borderline. There is a double-lumen 
central catheter in place which is unchanged from previous with 
the tip seen at the atriocaval junction. There is no evidence 
for pleural effusion or pneumothorax. The lung parenchyma is 
clear.

IMPRESSION: No evidence for acute congestive heart failure.

Card. Cath:
1. Selective coronary angiography of this right-dominant system 
demonstrated mild luminal irregularities in the LAD, RCA and 
LCX. No 
angiographically significant disease was seen. 
2. Limited hemodynamic assessment revealed normal systemic 
arterial 
blood pressure and moderately elevated LVEDP (21 mmHg). C areful 
pull 
back of the catheter showed no significant LV or transaortic 
gradient. 
3. Left ventriculography was deferred. 
  
FINAL DIAGNOSIS:     
1. Coronary arteries wihout obstructive disease. 
2. Moderately elevated left-sided filling pressures (LVEDP 21 
mmHg). 
3. No significant left ventricular or trans-aortic gradient.

TTE:
The left atrium is mildly dilated. There is severe symmetric 
left ventricular hypertrophy. The left ventricular cavity is 
unusually small. Left ventricular systolic function is 
hyperdynamic (EF>75%). Tissue Doppler imaging suggests an 
increased left ventricular filling pressure (PCWP>18mmHg). 
Transmitral Doppler and tissue velocity imaging are consistent 
with Grade II (moderate) LV diastolic dysfunction. There is a 
mild resting left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. The 
findings are consistent with hypertrophic obstructive 
cardiomyopathy (HOCM). There is no ventricular septal defect. 
Right ventricular chamber size and free wall motion are normal. 
The aortic valve leaflets (3) are mildly thickened but aortic 
stenosis is not present. No aortic regurgitation is seen. The 
mitral valve leaflets are mildly thickened. There is no mitral 
valve prolapse. There is no systolic anterior motion of the 
mitral valve leaflets. There is moderate functional mitral 
stenosis (mean gradient XXmmHg) due to mitral annular 
calcification. Trivial mitral regurgitation is seen. [Due to 
acoustic shadowing, the severity of mitral regurgitation may be 
significantly UNDERestimated.] The left ventricular inflow 
pattern suggests impaired relaxation. The estimated pulmonary 
artery systolic pressure is normal. There is no pericardial 
effusion. 

Compared with the prior study (images reviewed) of ___, 
the degree of LVH, outflow tract obstruction, mitral 
regurgitation are all similar. Left ventricular function appears 
hyperdynamic on the current study. The degree of mitral stenosis 
has increased slightly. There is no pericardial effusion seen on 
the current study.   

 
Brief Hospital Course:
#. CAD: The patient had no formal history of CAD but had a 
multitude of risk factors including PVD, DM, hyperlipidemia, 
smoking, and HTN. Initially it was thought that she had an 
NSTEMI at the OSH with the troponin elevations. However, cardiac 
catheterization showed relatively patent coronaries, making the 
negative stress test done at the OSH a true negative. It was 
felt that her troponin bumps were demand ischemia from her 
episodes of flutter. Her cardiac enzymes continued to trend down 
during her admission. She was continued on her home regimen of 
metoprolol, diltiazem, lisinopril, ASA, isordil and Zocor with 
good effect. She had no further episodes of shortness of breath, 
palpitations or chest pain while in hospital.  
.  
#. Rhythm: The patient has a history of paroxysmal atrial 
flutter, most recently having caused demand ischemia and 
pulmonary edema. She presented in NSR and remained there for the 
majority of her hospital stay. She did have one episode of rate 
controlled flutter during a hemodialysis session which ended 
spontaneously, with no elevations in her troponins. Out of 
concern for further complications related to her flutter, she 
received a caval-isthmus atrial flutter ablation. She returned 
from this procedure in normal sinus rhythm. However, after 
another hemodialysis session, she converted to a coarse atrial 
fibrillation that was rate controlled. She alternated between 
NSR and coarse atrial fibrillation. At that time, it was decided 
to medically manage her atrial fibrillation with rate control 
using metoprolol and diltiazem, and anticoagulation. Initially 
the patient did not desire to begin coumadin but was convinced 
to do so given the increased risk of stroke. She was initially 
anticoagulated using IV heparin and begun on 5mg coumadin daily. 
She will have her INR checked at hemodialysis and initially 
managed by her PCP, ___. Thereafter, management of 
her INR with be done the the ___ clinic. Her 
rate was well controlled with her home regimen of metoprolol and 
diltiazem. 
.  
#. Pump: She experienced an episode of acute pulmonary edema 
likely in setting of flutter as she has not had issues with 
fluid overload in the past and has had none since. Her EF on 
repeat TTE was normal. She was continued on her lisinopril and 
metoprolol with good effect
.
# UTI: The patient developed a mild leukocytosis on the day of 
discharge and had a positive urine analysis. She was begun on 
ciprofloxacin, renally dosed, for a total of a one week course. 
Urine culture grew out mixed genital flora. 
.  
# HOCM: Diagnosed on Echo in ___. However, the lack of flow 
gradient seen on cardiac catheterization excludes the diagnosis. 
She simply have LVH.  
.  
#. Hyperlipidemia: Continued on Zocor 80mg with good effect. 
Lipid panel checked here is within guidelines. 
.  
# ESRD: She continued to received her MWF hemodialysis with no 
ill effects. Her lanthanum was stopped as her phosphate was 
dropping on both the renagel and the lanthanum. Furthermore, 
there is better evidence that renagel is the superior phosphate 
binder. She was continued on her renagel and nephrocaps. She 
will follow up with her nephrologist.  
.  
# DM: Continued on her home dose NPH and covered with HISS  to 
good effect. 
.  
#. Code: FULL  
.

Discharge Condition:
All vital signs stable. Chest pain free. No arrhythmias on 
telemetry. 

 
Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted after you had trouble breathing. It seems that 
this trouble came from an abnormal rhythm in your heart called 
atrial flutter. This caused your heart rate to speed up and your 
heart to not pump as well, causing fluid to back up into your 
lungs. We found the place in your heart that was causing this 
abnormal rhythm and burned it to prevent it coming back. 
However, due to the increased risk of stroke if this rhythm does 
come back, we have started you on a blood thinning agent called 
Coumadin (warfarin). Your dialysis service will check your 
coumadin levels and fax the results to Dr. ___. The 
___ clinic will contact you on ___ to 
further manage your coumadin levels. 

You also had some elevations of the lab tests that showed some 
mild damage to your heart. This was not a heart attack. We 
evaluated your coronary arteries, the vessels that supply blood 
to the heart, and found no blockages. 

We have increased your lisinopril to better control your blood 
pressure. We have also stopped your lanthanum as you do not need 
it to control your phosphate levels. Please take all of your 
medications as prescribed and attend all of your follow up 
appointments. 

You were also found to have a mild urinary tract infection. You 
were begun on an antibiotic called Cipro to treat this. 
Please call your doctor or return to the emergency room if you 
experience chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, 
fevers, chills, bleeding, nausea, vomitting, or any other 
symptom that concerns you.
